transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Cardholder Services. My name is Marcus. How can I assist you today?

Customer: Hi Marcus, my name is Nathaniel Greer. I'm calling because my father, Walter Greer, passed away recently, and I was going through his records and saw a charge on his card that shouldn't be there.

Agent: I am very sorry for your loss, Mr. Greer. I can look into the account for you. To pull up the file, could you please provide your father's card number and his billing address?

Customer: Sure, the card number ends in 4109, and his home address was 2210 Birchwood Road in Fairview.

Agent: Thank you. And for verification purposes, could you provide his date of birth and the last four digits of his Social Security number?

Customer: Yes, his date of birth was March 14, 1948, and the last four of his Social are 8821.

Agent: Thank you, I have his profile in front of me now. Which transaction caught your attention?

Customer: It's from Elmstead Pharmacy on September 20th for $180.00.

Agent: I see that transaction for $180.00 on September 20th. Did your father regularly use Elmstead Pharmacy?

Customer: He picked up medication there a long time ago, but he was admitted to the hospital in early September and never came home, so he couldn't have been at the store.

Agent: Did anyone else have physical access to his card, or did he give anyone permission to pick up items on his behalf during that time?

Customer: No, his wallet was locked away in the hospital administration safe the whole time, and nobody had permission to use his cards.

Agent: Have you spoken with Elmstead Pharmacy to ask about the transaction?

Customer: I did call them a few days ago, but the person on the phone said they couldn't give me any information about the receipt because the account was in his name.

Agent: All right, I understand. So to make sure I have everything noted correctly, you are reporting this $180.00 charge from Elmstead Pharmacy on September 20th because your father, Walter Greer, was in the hospital at the time, his card was locked away, and nobody else had permission to use it.

Customer: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
